scenes.visual: A strawberry runner makes a copy; two siblings differ; the question appears.
scenes.tts: A strawberry plant sends a thin stem along the ground. Where it touches soil, it can grow roots. It becomes a new plant with the same genetic information as its parent. Brothers and sisters have the same two parents, and they usually look different. Why don't you look exactly like your parents, or like your brothers and sisters?

scenes.visual: Asexual column: one parent, same offspring. Sexual column: two sex cells join into offspring.
scenes.tts: A runner is asexual reproduction. It has one parent. The offspring, the new living things, are genetically the same as the parent. Sexual reproduction is different. Two sex cells join, usually one from each of two parents. The offspring resemble their parents, but they are not copies.

scenes.visual: Model body cell with two pairs; pair bracket; mother and father tags; human numbers; copy; count stays four.
scenes.tts: In a body cell, such as a skin cell, chromosomes come in pairs. A chromosome pair is two matching chromosomes. One comes from your mother, and one from your father. A typical human body cell has forty-six chromosomes, in twenty-three pairs. In most males, the X and Y chromosomes form a pair even though they match only in small parts. Before a cell divides to make sex cells, each chromosome is copied. A copied chromosome is still one chromosome.
scenes.narration: In a body cell, such as a skin cell, chromosomes come in pairs. A chromosome pair is two matching chromosomes. One comes from your mother, and one from your father. A typical human body cell has 46 chromosomes, in 23 pairs. In most males, the X and Y chromosomes form a pair even though they match only in small parts. Before a cell divides to make sex cells, each chromosome is copied. A copied chromosome is still one chromosome.

scenes.visual: Parent cell with four chromosomes goes through meiosis to a sex cell with two, one from each pair; human line.
scenes.tts: Meiosis is the cell division that makes sex cells. Each sex cell gets one chromosome from each pair. So it has half of the parent's chromosomes. A human egg or sperm normally has twenty-three chromosomes.
scenes.narration: Meiosis is the cell division that makes sex cells. Each sex cell gets one chromosome from each pair. So it has half of the parent's chromosomes. A human egg or sperm normally has 23 chromosomes.

scenes.visual: Parent cell with B and b; two sex cells with different mixes; 50 percent labels.
scenes.tts: Each pair splits up on its own, without regard to the other pairs. So each sex cell gets a mix chosen by chance. An allele is one version of a gene. Say a parent has alleles big B and little b. Each sex cell has a fifty percent chance of carrying B. It has the same chance of carrying little b.

scenes.visual: Egg and sperm join to full pairs; two children with different mixes; runner plant identical to parent.
scenes.tts: Fertilization joins a sperm and an egg into one new cell. In humans, twenty-three chromosomes plus twenty-three make forty-six. The fertilized egg has full pairs again, one from each parent. Each child grows from a different egg and sperm. Sex cells carry different mixes, so brothers and sisters usually differ. A runner has one parent, so it is genetically the same.
